solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of church where tense parents dither

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: to dither is to be flustered and all over the place, so the letters of parents are jumbled

explanation.surface: In a church, a couple of anxious parents can't decide where to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like the anxious parents' mood, but it is the grammar term; 'where' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the crosswise arm of a cruciform church building.

clue.text: Part of feeding involves sticky stuff

indicators.note: the phrase involves, or contains, the run of letters spanning its words

explanation.surface: One aspect of feeding a child involves sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like the selection signal, but the run spans 'parT OF FEEding' and 'involves' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy, sticky confection of boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Canvas covering a new extension outside

indicators.note: the extension sits outside the new, enclosing it

parts.note: an extension to a building is a wing

explanation.surface: A canvas cover going up over a newly built extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a sheet of canvas stretched over a doorway or window for shade.

clue.text: Servile, small and sumptuous

parts.note: sumptuous means lavish

explanation.surface: A list of contrasting qualities in a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish means submissive and servile, like a slave.

clue.text: Pressure's on ex-bride (old one) coiffed like Diana Dors?

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: hair coiffed is styled and rearranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A divorced woman of a certain age has her hair styled like a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links P to the jumble. Diana Dors was a 1950s British film star known for bleached hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana Dors was famous for her bleached peroxide hair, the archetypal artificial blonde.

clue.text: Make them to compensate people in commercials

indicators.note: people sit in commercials, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: commercials are adverts, ADS for short
people as a plural, MEN

explanation.surface: An instruction to put people into advertisements to make up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'make amends': 'them' stands for the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is the idiom for offering compensation or reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: Study hard sticky stuff?

parts.note: sticky stuff is gum, and in a down entry that word written upwards appears as the answer's first word followed by up

explanation.surface: A question whether hard study is a sticky business.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: its first word, written upwards in a down light, is a sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is a British idiom for cramming or studying intensively.

clue.text: Harmless drunk on tonic gets cross

indicators.note: the jumble gets, or takes in, the cross inside it
drunk letters stagger out of order, so on tonic is rearranged

parts.note: a cross is shaped like the letter X

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker on gin and tonic turns angry yet stays harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles ON TONIC into NONTOIC, which 'gets' X inside it; 'cross' looks like angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-toxic means not poisonous, and so harmless to health.

clue.text: Technologically advanced gap years?

parts.note: a gap is a space
a long period of years is an age

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gap year is a high-tech thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gap years' suggests a student's year off, but the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something very modern or futuristic in technology.

clue.text: Rolf made yellow bananas for children's game

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Rolf, a TV entertainer, turned bananas yellow for kids' amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit in the surface but signals the letters of ROLF MADE YELLOW go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Follow-my-leader is a children's game in which everyone copies the one in front.

clue.text: Swings and roundabouts not just on Fair Head

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the Fair piece goes first
the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Fair is taken

parts.note: something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: A remark that things are unjust at Fair Head, a headland in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: UNFAIR sits 'on' (after) F, the head of Fair. Fair Head is a real cliff on the Antrim coast, which hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Swings and roundabouts are the typical rides found at a travelling fairground.

clue.text: Stuff soldiers and navy into strip

parts.note: OR means other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: navy is put into the strip, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Gaza Strip, so strip gives GAZA

explanation.surface: Troops and sailors being sent into a narrow territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is the noun meaning fabric, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin stiff sheer fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: 9 drift round youth centre in boredom

indicators.note: the jumbled number goes round the next piece, enclosing it
to drift is to wander out of place, so the letters of nine move around

parts.note: the number 9 is spelt out as the word nine

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here of youth

explanation.surface: A listless young person wandering about a youth club in tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drift' turns NINE into ENNI, and 'round' puts U, the centre of youth, inside it; '9' is a number, not a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for weary listlessness and tedium.

clue.text: Two unknowns help Ono to play this?

definitions.text: Two unknowns help Ono to play this?

parts.note: x and y are the unknowns of algebra

indicators.note: to play the letters is to arrange them anew, so help Ono is jumbled

explanation.surface: Yoko Ono getting help from two mystery people to perform on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of Ono playing the instrument, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument played with mallets, which Ono might play.

clue.text: TV stops secretly following practice in ring

indicators.note: the TV stops up, or plugs, the gap in the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: secretly following someone is shadowing them
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A detective stops tailing a suspect because of the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like 'halts' but means 'plugs', and 'TV' is the box, as in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise by sparring against an imaginary opponent, which is called shadow-boxing.

clue.text: Sailor's pamphlet is not material

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, here with the possessive S
a tract is a pamphlet

explanation.surface: A seaman's leaflet is said to be irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract describes something that exists as an idea rather than as physical matter.

clue.text: Child's on board earlier ship

indicators.note: being on board means being inside, so child goes within the other word

parts.note: earlier means sooner
CH is the abbreviation for child, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: A child had boarded a vessel earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's' means 'child is': CH is on board SOONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts.

clue.text: It cryptically suggests 500 could get lost there

definitions.text: It cryptically suggests 500 could get lost there

parts.words: It cryptically suggests 500 could get lost there
parts.note: the Roman numeral for 500 is D, the last letter of a word meaning further away, and a remote place is where anyone could get lost

explanation.surface: A place so remote that 500 people might wander off there.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read literally names the final letter of 'beyond', which is D, the Roman 500.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of beyond is an idiom for a very remote, out-of-the-way place.

clue.text: Greek character solved crime to do with figures

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: a puzzle solved is worked out, so crime is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek man solved a crime by doing the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeric means relating to numbers or expressed in numbers.

clue.text: Shakespearean carpenter's question in church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A carpenter from Shakespeare poses a question in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Quince is the carpenter who directs the play in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Quince is the carpenter among the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Check about Scottish sweetheart's return

indicators.note: the check goes about the sweetheart, surrounding it

parts.note: to check a horse is to rein it in
jo is Scots for a sweetheart, as in Burns's John Anderson, my Jo

explanation.surface: A Scotswoman checking on her lover coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' is the noun or verb for a reply, not coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin is to reply sharply, giving a return to a remark.

clue.text: In the most woeful setting ducks are attractive

indicators.note: the jumbled letters form a setting around the ducks, enclosing them
woeful means badly off, signalling the letters of the most are scrambled

parts.note: a duck is a nought in cricket, so ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: Ducks look appealing in the gloomiest of surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woeful' scrambles THE MOST into TTHSME order around OO; a duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty, and by extension appealing or sexually attractive.

clue.text: Composer hadn't time left to tackle end of symphony

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, so the shortened word grips the next letter
time left means it departed, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, without its apostrophe

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A composer ran out of time to finish his symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes T from HADNT to leave HADN, which tackles Y, the end of symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian composer known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: How to work American/English PC device

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

explanation.surface: Asking how to operate a computer device on either side of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is the hand-held pointer used to control a personal computer.

clue.text: Anyone in trouble with duke is put out

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so anyone is rearranged

explanation.surface: Anybody who crosses the duke ends up displeased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is an idiom for being irritated or upset.

clue.text: Couple called in Mexican city

indicators.note: called is placed in the couple, inside it

parts.note: a couple is a pair or duo
called on the phone, rang

explanation.surface: A pair telephoned from a city in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Durango is a city and state capital in north-west Mexico.

clue.text: Elizabeth replaced George in large crowd on it

definitions.text: Elizabeth replaced George in large crowd on it

indicators.note: one person replaced another, so one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: a large crowd is a throng
G is the initial of George
E is the initial of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth succeeded King George and sat on the royal seat.
explanation.walkthrough: In THRONG the G for George becomes E for Elizabeth; the whole clue recalls Elizabeth II succeeding George VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The throne is the monarch's ceremonial seat, on which Elizabeth followed George.

clue.text: Launder proceeds of larceny led by director

indicators.note: the director comes first, leading the other piece
proceeds suggests what larceny is turned into, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A film director laundering the money from a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds of' rearranges LARCENY into RYCLEAN; 'led by' puts D first. 'Launder' hints at money laundering but means wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry-clean clothes is to launder them using solvent instead of water.
